title: CREATE DATABASE
description: Learn how to create a new database in SQL Server using the CREATE DATABASE statement.

data.text: The CREATE DATABASE statement creates a new database in SQL Server. The database name must be unique within an instance of SQL Server and comply with SQL Server identifier rules, typically with a maximum of 128 characters.

data.title: Basic CREATE DATABASE Syntax
data.content: Creates a new database with the specified name.

data.text: The following statement creates a new database named TestDb:

data.title: Create TestDb Database
data.content: Creates a new database named TestDb.

data.text: Once the statement executes successfully, you can view the newly created database in the Object Explorer. If the database does not appear, you can click the Refresh button or press F5 to update the object list.

data.alt: SQL Server CREATE DATABASE example showing the new database in Object Explorer

data.text: You can list all databases using a query against the system catalog:

data.title: List All Databases
data.content: Queries all database names from the system catalog.
data.code:
SELECT
    name
FROM
    master.sys.databases
ORDER BY
    name;

data.text: Alternatively, you can use the stored procedure sp_databases:

data.title: Using sp_databases
data.content: Lists all databases using the sp_databases stored procedure.

data.text: You can also create a database using SQL Server Management Studio:

items: Right-click the Database folder and choose New Database…
Enter the name of the database (e.g., SampleDb) and click OK
The newly created database appears in the Object Explorer under the Databases node

data.alt: SQL Server CREATE DATABASE using SSMS step 1

data.title: CREATE DATABASE Key Points
points: Use CREATE DATABASE to create a new database in SQL Server.
The database name must be unique within the SQL Server instance.
You can list databases using sys.databases or sp_databases.
SQL Server Management Studio provides a graphical way to create databases.
